title: One call, still being answered
note: The page's paths converging from every direction on the House, under the word labbayk, here I am.

lines.text: Hajj is Islam's fifth pillar, and a call
The House, once in a life, in Dhul Hijjah
lines.sub: for whoever can find a way there

lines.text: Ibrahim was told to make the call
One man called out in an empty valley
lines.sub: every crowd since has been the echo

lines.text: You answer labbayk: here I am
The verse says whoever is able, just once

lines.sub: Shafi'is, Hanbalis: he must send someone

lines.text: The accepted Hajj's only reward: Paradise
One call still being answered today
lines.src: The fifth pillar, and its verse

research.retell: Hajj is Islam's fifth pillar, a single call Ibrahim was told to make in an empty valley, and every pilgrim still answers it by saying labbayk, here I am, once in a lifetime.
proof: Islam is built on five things, and the fifth is Hajj to the House for whoever can find a way to it.; one call, made in an empty valley, still being answered
to Allah, from the people, is a pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to find a way there.

Allah settled Ibrahim at the place of the House and told him to purify it for those who circle it, and then to proclaim the pilgrimage to the people; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, from every distant mountain pass
One man called out in an empty valley. Every crowd since has been the echo.
the first thing you say when you enter ihram is not a request but an answer. Labbayk. Here I am. The word is a reply to a call, and the call is older than every person in the crowd around you.
The verse does not say every year, and it does not say everyone. It says whoever is able, once.; Everything after that is a gift you give, not a debt you pay.

Hanafi and Maliki hold that a person unable to travel because of permanent illness is not obliged in himself... Shafi’i and Hanbali hold that the one who is permanently unable in body but able in wealth must have someone perform Hajj on his behalf.
the accepted Hajj, al-Hajj al-mabrur, has no reward except Paradise.
